riskNotes.note: Agent-supplied `config` with an absolute-path `extends` executed arbitrary JS in 0.1.3; fixed in 0.1.4. Verified by execution (lint_solidity, absolute path) and at source (array, solhint:../, plugins, fix_solidity). Unchanged in 0.1.7.
Linting, or reading the config with get_config, runs that repository's own Solhint plugins and JS config, the same trust as running `npx solhint` there. Not safe for untrusted repositories.

Run health (C4) resolved in 0.1.7: a plugin that fails to load or an unknown rule id is reported as a "⚠️ This run was degraded" banner naming each problem, above the findings, also with FORCE_COLOR set; get_config no longer claims the config is sound. A degraded run is not isError (by design: findings from the rules that did load stay usable), so the agent must read the banner. Verified by execution: lint-stage cases 21/21 on 0.1.7 (CI, 2026-10-24; SCORECARD.md §2.4d).

components.scorecardRef: SCORECARD.md §1 (Build / test row); §2.5 (build/test-stage cases: 22/22 on forge 1.8.5 and 1.8.6, CI 2026-10-26)

riskNotes.note: Running tests runs the project's code: forge test executes its Solidity and cheatcodes with the user's privileges, the same trust as running forge test there. Not safe for untrusted repositories.

FFI is off unless the server is started with --allow-ffi (a user setting, not a tool argument), even when foundry.toml sets ffi = true. Verified by execution: the FFI command never runs (SCORECARD.md §2.5b). Tests can still reach the network through fork cheatcodes or rpc_endpoints if the project configures them.

Results redact the exact values of variables named like PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, SECRET, TOKEN, API_KEY or RPC_URL, from the environment and the project's .env (hex with or without 0x, and decimal). A secret under another name, or one a test transforms before printing, is not caught.
